verdict.demonstrated_behavior: Exit 3 is the supervisor's deliberate sanitized failure mapping, not a unique crash diagnosis. Loss of current lease, schema/DB availability or runtime exchange can reach it even with no native/model work.
verdict.product_journey: BLOCKED before native preparation; no new profile, deadline enlargement, service retry or mutation authorized by this report

observations.other_services: API, DB and runtime containers running at parent's observation, not proof of healthy control or live native work

parent_supplied_readonly_db.provenance: Parent reported exact-owned DB BEGIN READ ONLY / ROLLBACK, exit 0; not repeated by this reviewer

observations.diagnostics_limit: Parent reports only finite READY/UNAVAILABLE log markers and no matching suspend/timejump/OOM journal pattern in its bounded window. Raw logs were not read or printed. Neither expiry time nor absence of matching journal entries proves the initiating cause.

findings.claim: The normal supervisor has no total idle-lifetime expiry. Every approximately one-second cycle rechecks schema, heartbeats the DB lease, quiesces and requests runtime status. IDLE is accepted in the normal non-probe branch. A raised error escapes the loop and reaches exit 3; no generic reconnect/retry exists there.

A runtime stream read gap exceeding 2.5 seconds makes RuntimeHost emit RUNTIME_DENIED with id=null. The next client exchange requires its own request id, so it rejects the uncorrelated frame, closes the channel and raises RuntimeUnavailable. Ordinary exchanges also have a 2-second timeout. The supervisor normally sends status each one-second cycle; no observation proves such a gap or timeout occurred in UI9.
findings.existing_test_limit: Existing held-idle/released-same-boot real-UDS regression was inspected, not executed because it creates IPC/private runtime metadata outside this read-only task. It does not establish this incident's cause.

findings.claim: SUPERVISOR_UNAVAILABLE merges OSError, ValueError (including RuntimeUnavailable), TimeoutError, SQLAlchemyError and domain conflicts. Cleanup can replace the first error: failed runtime drain raises before service.release. Thus owner_present=true with an expired lease is compatible with, but does not identify, several paths; exit 3 and the current DB row cannot select one.

Existing Start cannot recover this READY journal with an exited supervisor. It takes verify_running, which requires every recorded service Running=true and refuses with RECOVERY_REQUIRED/4. No restart subcommand exists; restart.py is only the internal STOPPED-to-Start reconciliation path.

Existing Stop attempts verify_running first. With this failed service it enters emergency Stop, durably marks UNCERTAIN/unreconciled before inventory/drain and returns failure. That path removes only exactly attested resources and preserves PGDATA, but does not manufacture FINALIZE/STOPPED or provide a supported next Start. It may also refuse before teardown if exact identity/IPC checks fail. Do not run stop merely as a recovery experiment.

The data-preserving normal path is verified SHUTDOWN, quiescence, FINALIZE, Stop grant and COMPLETED host receipt, then STOPPED and a new explicit Start with DB-only reconciliation ACK before supervisor acquisition/OPEN. Current READY/exited control has no such receipt. Reusing stop_reconcile requires that authentic grant/completion; absence of native work does not create it. Direct supervisor restart would acquire a new epoch and, if admission is open, close/increment its generation, rather than restore the journal's old authority.

Catalog confirmation is a persistent operator-confirmation record bound to owner, exact selection and catalog head, not supervisor epoch/boot. There is no reason to repeat the human confirmation solely because the supervisor died. Normal restart retains existing PGDATA/catalog directories; emergency containment does not intentionally delete them. However survival is not a demonstrated recovery to READY. Native preparation still needs the live current supervisor owner and IDLE runtime, and the same-instance source record is presently absent per parent.

exact_missing_observation.historical_cause: The FIRST failing producer/await phase and its allowlisted exception type/domain code before RuntimeClient normalization and supervisor finally: schema read, lease heartbeat/quiesce, runtime status/renew, or cleanup. For a timeout/idle-gap claim, the corresponding observed DB-clock lease check and monotonic frame/response interval are also missing. Existing finite log markers and current expired lease do not reconstruct them.
exact_missing_observation.recovery: This is not waiting for another broad log/query: the supported lifecycle has no transition from the observed READY journal plus dead supervisor to reconciled READY without authentic completed Stop authority. The parent already supplied the minimum read-only DB facts; no duplicate DB/log reads are proposed.

minimum_next_decision.recommendation: Keep UI9 data/catalog/confirmation and the failure evidence unchanged. Decide explicitly whether to authorize a narrowly scoped same-instance crash-recovery procedure/product slice with verified backup/restore and durable reconciliation, or leave this journey BLOCKED. Do not replace the installation/profile or pretend normal Stop-to-Start is currently admissible.
minimum_next_decision.scope_if_authorized: Only original UI9 identities/PGDATA/catalog and existing owners; establish exact state and no unresolved work, preserve confirmation/head/source, reconcile new lease/generation plus host journal before OPEN, prove readiness/readback, then resume Publish -> native preparation -> normal Stop/Start -> Test model. This is a contract decision and future work, not an existing executable command or authorization from this report.
minimum_next_decision.containment_warning: NOT EXECUTED and NOT a recovery recommendation. Expected current branch is emergency UNCERTAIN/RECOVERY_REQUIRED, possibly partial/no teardown if attestation fails, and future ordinary Start remains blocked.
